Sharpee

bibl.title: Associative learning enhances population coding by inverting inter-neuronal correlation patterns

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how associative learning changes the pattern of correlations between neurons, and what that does to population coding
span.quote: Learning-dependent cortical encoding has been well described in single neurons. But behaviorally relevant sensory signals drive the coordinated activity of millions of cortical neurons; whether learning produces stimulus specific changes in population codes is unknown.

span.label: whether learning acts on emergent population properties that cannot be observed in single neurons
span.quote: In contrast, little is known about how, or even if, learning might act on the neural ensemble representations by changing emergent properties not observable in single neurons.

span.label: shows learning inverts the relationship between signal and noise correlations, but only for stimuli that guide behaviour, and that this improves population decoding increasingly with population size
span.quote: We show that learning produces stimulus specific changes in the pattern of inter-neuronal correlations that enhance the ability of neural populations to recognize signals relevant for behavior. This learning-dependent enhancement increases with population size.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We show that learning produces stimulus specific changes in the pattern of inter-neuronal correlations that enhance the ability of neural populations to recognize signals relevant for behavior.

span.label: inter-neuronal noise correlations in population coding
span.quote: Here, we examine how associative learning influences the stimulus-specific pattern of inter-neuronal correlations and encoding among neural ensembles in a high-level auditory region in the songbird brain.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: After training, we recorded the simultaneous activity of multiple well-isolated single neurons in the caudolateral mesopallium (CLM) in response to task-relevant and task-irrelevant motifs and a third set of novel motifs under urethane anesthesia ( Supplemental Figure S2A-P ; Experimental Procedures).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: when noise correlation runs opposite to tuning similarity, a downstream reader can subtract the responses of dissimilarly tuned neurons, cancelling the shared noise while adding the signal, so the same spikes carry more information
span.quote: In contrast, negative relationships can improve population coding because common noise among dissimilarly tuned neurons can be subtracted, which strengthens the signal while dissipating the noise.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: learning-driven changes to feed-forward synaptic weights (with excitatory-inhibitory noise cancellation) decorrelate similarly tuned neurons and preserve or increase correlation among dissimilarly tuned ones, producing the inverted correlation structure
span.quote: The plausibility of such circuitry is supported by a recent network model showing that learning-driven modulations to feed-forward synaptic weights yields decreased noise correlations for similarly tuned cortical neurons, and increased noise correlations for dissimilarly tuned neurons

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the trigger for the correlation change is the learned stimulus-to-action mapping (the motif signalling which port to peck), not reward pairing, familiarity or exposure, which were equated across motif classes
span.quote: Thus, learning-dependent changes in the inter-neuronal correlation patterns depend on associations formed between stimuli and behavior, rather than experience, familiarity, or reward contingency.

span.label: positively correlated noise between similarly tuned neurons impairs coding because pooling cannot remove shared noise without removing signal
span.quote: Compared to independent noise, positively correlated noise between two similarly tuned neurons impairs encoding because no form of response pooling can attenuate the shared noise without simultaneously attenuating the signal

span.label: positively correlated noise between oppositely tuned neurons improves coding because subtraction removes noise and strengthens signal
span.quote: In contrast, positively correlated noise between two oppositely tuned neurons can improve encoding because subtracting one response from the other can both attenuate the shared noise and strengthen the signal

span.label: trial shuffling separates the contribution of single-neuron plasticity from that of correlation change, since it leaves individual responses untouched
span.quote: To distinguish these two sources of increased performance, we compared the classification performance without correlations (i.e. with trials shuffled, which does not alter individual neuron responses) to that with correlations intact.

span.label: the design equalises reward across all trained motifs so only the stimulus-response association differs
span.quote: All the motifs used during training were heard equally often in the context of the task and paired equally with reinforcement, but only the task-relevant motifs signaled the correct behavioral response on each trial. Thus, any effect of learning mediated directly by reinforcement should apply to all of the training motifs.

span.label: testing each motif in isolation confirms the behavioural asymmetry is about which response the motif signals, not about reward
span.quote: As expected, each of the single task-relevant motifs evoked responses primarily to a single port, following the learned responses from training ( Figure 1E ). In contrast, responses to the task-irrelevant motifs were evenly distributed between both response ports ( Figure 1E ). Importantly, overall response rates for all the motifs were similarly high

span.label: The narrow-spiking (putative interneuron) sample was too small for reliable pair analysis, so the population results rest on wide-spiking pairs only.
span.note: what this limits: every pairwise-correlation result: WE FOCUS ON WS NEURONS ... BECAUSE OUR SAMPLE OF NS NEURONS WAS NOT SUFFICIENT (N = 17 PAIRS FROM 36 SINGLE NEURONS) TO PERFORM RELIABLE ANA[lysis]
span.quote: We focus on WS neurons (n = 176 pairs from 98 single neurons) because our sample of NS neurons was not sufficient (n = 17 pairs from 36 single neurons) to perform reliable analysis.

span.label: The claim that correlation-structure plasticity is confined to putative excitatory neurons is underpowered.
span.note: what this limits: the cell-type specificity claim specifically: THIS SUGGESTS THAT THE PLASTICITY ... PRIMARILY EXISTS WITHIN WS (PUTATIVE EXCITATORY) NEURONS, ALTHOUGH MORE DATA ARE NECESSARY - the negative half rests on the underpowered sample
span.quote: This suggests that the plasticity of the correlation structure primarily exists within WS (putative excitatory) neurons, although more data are necessary.

span.label: Recordings were made under urethane anaesthesia, unlike the awake comparison study, and the circuitry producing the stimulus-specific flexibility is not identified.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison with the awake primate study: A METHODOLOGICAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN OUR STUDY AND THAT OF (GU, ET. AL. 2011) IS THAT WE USED ANESTHETIZED ANIMALS WHILE GU AND COLLEAGUES USED AWAKE ANIMALS
span.quote: A methodological difference between our study and that of ( Gu, et. al. 2011 ) is that we used anesthetized animals while Gu and colleagues used awake animals.

span.label: The local or extrinsic circuit mechanism controlling the correlation structure remains to be established.
span.note: what this limits: any circuit account of the effect: FURTHER EXPERIMENTS WILL BE NECESSARY TO ELUCIDATE THE CIRCUITRY THAT YIELDS THIS STIMULUS-SPECIFIC FLEXIBILITY
span.quote: Further experiments will be necessary to elucidate the circuitry that yields this stimulus-specific flexibility.

span.label: narrow-spiking neurons were excluded because the sample was too small for reliable analysis
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - narrow-spiking neurons were excluded because the sample was too small for reliable analysis, so the population results are the broad-spiking ones
span.quote: We focus on WS neurons (n = 176 pairs from 98 single neurons) because our sample of NS neurons was not sufficient (n = 17 pairs from 36 single neurons) to perform reliable analysis.

span.label: recordings were made under urethane anaesthesia, unlike the study whose result this contradicts
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, with the authors' position: WE THINK IT IS HIGHLY UNLIKELY THAT ANESTHESIA COULD ACCOUNT FOR THE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN OUR RESULTS FOR TWO REASONS
span.quote: A methodological difference between our study and that of ( Gu, et. al. 2011 ) is that we used anesthetized animals while Gu and colleagues used awake animals. We think it is highly unlikely that anesthesia could account for the differences between our results for two reasons.

span.label: the single-neuron firing rate difference is modest relative to the behavioural change it accompanies
span.note: what this limits: any single-neuron reading of the learning effect: THE MODULATION OF SINGLE NEURON FIRING RATES IS SUBTLE ... ESPECIALLY IN LIGHT OF THE ANIMALS' ROBUST CHANGES IN BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE
span.quote: The modulation of single neuron firing rates is subtle, however, especially in light of the animals’ robust changes in behavioral performance over training ( Figure 1D ) and differential responding to relevant and irrelevant motifs after training

span.label: the effect in pairs of neurons is described as modest, and only grows large in bigger populations
span.note: what this limits: the size of the correlation effect at the scale it was measured: A MODEST EFFECT IN PAIRS OF NEURONS GROWS CONSIDERABLY WITH POPULATION SIZE, and for irrelevant motifs the effect IS SMALL AND DOES NOT DEPEND ON POPULATION SIZE
span.quote: We find that the effect of correlations on coding of task-irrelevant and novel motifs is small and does not depend on population size; in contrast, for task-relevant motifs, a modest effect in pairs of neurons grows considerably with population size

span.label: the comparison with the contradicting study differs in species, brain region, sensory modality and type of learning
span.note: what this limits: the disagreement with the primate study, whose differing parameters are enumerated: THIS STUDY DIFFERED FROM OURS IN MULTIPLE WAYS (E.G. SPECIES, BRAIN REGION, AND SENSORY MODALITY) and type of learning
span.quote: Indeed, a recent study found that perceptual learning did not alter the slope of the relationship between signal and noise correlations for neurons in the primate medial superior temporal area ( Gu et al., 2011 ). This study differed from ours in multiple ways (e.g. species, brain region, and sensory modality) that make direct comparisons difficult, but one important difference is in the type of learning.

span.label: the concept of 'occasion setting' is imported to reinterpret the CLM motif representation as a predictive mapping onto the learned response rather than a sensory trace
span.quote: In this context, which psychologists refer to as occasion setting ( Schmajuk and Holland, 1998 ), we suggest that the neural representation of motifs in CLM is less a sensory trace than a predictive mapping of the learned behavioral response.

span.label: occasion setting - the idea that a stimulus signals which response is appropriate rather than predicting reward itself - used to reinterpret what the cortical representation is for
span.quote: In this context, which psychologists refer to as occasion setting ( Schmajuk and Holland, 1998 ), we suggest that the neural representation of motifs in CLM is less a sensory trace than a predictive mapping of the learned behavioral response.

span.label: multinomial logistic regression, chosen because stimulus identity is categorical and cannot be parameterised
span.quote: Because motif identity is best regarded as a nominal, or categorical, variable (i.e. motifs cannot be easily described with a small number of parameters), we use multinomial logistic regression (MNLR) to find the optimal classifier that maximizes the predictability of motif identity from the firing rates of multiple neurons (Experimental Procedures). This technique is particularly well-suited to our data because it can be applied to any number of neurons and any number of nominal categories (i.e. motifs).

span.label: the trial-shuffling repeated 50 times, with the AVERAGE classification probability used rather than a single shuffle
span.quote: To ensure that random correlations introduced by this process did not affect our analysis, we repeated the shuffling process 50 times and used the average probability of correct classification from these shuffles.

span.label: noise correlation is shared trial-to-trial variability; signal correlation is tuning similarity - and the coding consequence of the first depends entirely on the sign of the second
span.quote: In such circuits, noise correlations can either enhance or impair coding fidelity, depending on how the noise correlation relates to tuning similarity (known as “signal correlation”) for each pair of neurons

span.label: task-relevant means the motif signalled which response was correct; task-irrelevant motifs were equally familiar and equally rewarded, so relevance here is purely a stimulus-response association
span.quote: All the motifs used during training were heard equally often in the context of the task and paired equally with reinforcement, but only the task-relevant motifs signaled the correct behavioral response on each trial. Thus, any effect of learning mediated directly by reinforcement should apply to all of the training motifs.

span.label: the classification ratio is defined so that above one means correlations help and below one means they hurt, making the sign of the effect readable directly
span.quote: We expressed this potential benefit as the “classification ratio,” which is simply the ratio of the MNLR classification accuracy with correlations intact to the classification accuracy without correlations (i.e. with trials shuffled, Experimental Procedures). Classification ratios greater than one indicate that correlations improve encoding while classification ratios less than one indicate that correlations impair encoding.

span.label: the CLM representation is interpreted as a predictive mapping of the learned response rather than a sensory trace - occasion setting rather than encoding
span.quote: In this context, which psychologists refer to as occasion setting ( Schmajuk and Holland, 1998 ), we suggest that the neural representation of motifs in CLM is less a sensory trace than a predictive mapping of the learned behavioral response.

span.label: claim_type: mechanism
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: To our knowledge, a negative relationship between signal and noise correlations has not previously been demonstrated. Theoretical studies, however, have predicted that changes to the sign of this relationship might underlie cognitive functions such as attention or learning ( Oram et al., 1998 ). We thus provide the first evidence to support this prediction: associative learning inverts this relationship, substantially enhancing population encoding of learned motifs.

span.label: method: two-alternative operant training on song motifs, then simultaneous recording of up to 8 neurons and multinomial logistic regression decoding with and without trial shuffling
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Because motif identity is best regarded as a nominal, or categorical, variable (i.e. motifs cannot be easily described with a small number of parameters), we use multinomial logistic regression (MNLR) to find the optimal classifier that maximizes the predictability of motif identity from the firing rates of multiple neurons (Experimental Procedures). This technique is particularly well-suited to our data because it can be applied to any number of neurons and any number of nominal categories (i.e. motifs).

span.label: phenomenon: learning-dependent plasticity of inter-neuronal correlation structure
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: inter-neuronal noise correlations in population coding — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Thus, the relationship between the signal and the noise correlations acts in a stimulus specific way to enhance the representation of only those signals made relevant by prior learning.

span.label: builds-on → Oram et al. (1998)
span.quote: Our results support the longstanding hypothesis that these activity patterns underlie behaviorally relevant discrimination of sensory signals ( Oram et al., 1998 ).

span.label: replicates → Cohen and Kohn (2011); Gu et al. (2011); Kohn and Smith (2005); Zohary et al. (1994)
span.quote: Consistent with previous reports ( Cohen and Kohn, 2011 ; Gu et al., 2011 ; Kohn and Smith, 2005 ; Zohary et al., 1994 ), we observed broad distributions of noise correlations that had small, but positive, mean values (task-relevant: 0.082 ± 0.012; task-irrelevant: 0.100 ± 0.012; novel: 0.087 ± 0.012; Figure 3A ).

span.label: replicates → Jeanne et al. (2011); Gentner and Margoliash (2003); Thompson and Gentner (2010)
span.quote: This finding is consistent with previous reports that song recognition learning alters encoding by single neurons in CLM ( Jeanne et al., 2011 ) and neighboring regions ( Gentner and Margoliash, 2003 ; Thompson and Gentner, 2010 ).

span.label: contradicts → the inference from earlier work that stimulus-reward association drives auditory cortical plasticity
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS TASK RELEVANCE OF THE STIMULUS. 'ONLY THE TASK-RELEVANT motifs - those that birds learned to associate with a particular pecking location - elicited neural population activity with a NEGATIVE relationship between signal and noise correlations. In contrast, task-irrelevant motifs ... elicited neural population activi[ty]' [with the opposite sign]. The sign of the correlation relationship depends on learned relevance, so a claim about signal-noise correlations is only well-formed once the stimulus class is stated. Q-447.
span.quote: What we observe, however, is very different. Only the task-relevant—motifs those that birds learned to associate with a particular pecking location—elicited neural population activity with a negative relationship between signal and noise correlations. In contrast, task-irrelevant motifs—those that birds never learned to associate with a particular pecking location—elicited neural population activity with a positive correlation relationship indistinguishable from that elicited by novel motifs that birds never heard while awake. Thus, learning-dependent changes in the inter-neuronal correlation patterns depend on associations formed between stimuli and behavior, rather than experience, familiarity, or reward contingency.

span.label: confirms → the theoretical prediction that changing the sign of the signal-noise correlation relationship could underlie attention or learning
span.quote: To our knowledge, a negative relationship between signal and noise correlations has not previously been demonstrated. Theoretical studies, however, have predicted that changes to the sign of this relationship might underlie cognitive functions such as attention or learning ( Oram et al., 1998 ). We thus provide the first evidence to support this prediction: associative learning inverts this relationship, substantially enhancing population encoding of learned motifs.

span.label: qualifies → Gu et al., who found perceptual learning did not alter the slope of this relationship
span.quote: Indeed, a recent study found that perceptual learning did not alter the slope of the relationship between signal and noise correlations for neurons in the primate medial superior temporal area ( Gu et al., 2011 ). This study differed from ours in multiple ways (e.g. species, brain region, and sensory modality) that make direct comparisons difficult, but one important difference is in the type of learning.

span.label: supports → theoretical work showing correlations help when signal and noise correlations have opposite sign
span.quote: Thus, our data demonstrate that the observed correlations improve encoding when signal and noise correlations are of opposite sign and impair encoding when signal and noise correlations are of the same sign (2-way ANOVA interaction term, p = 1.8

span.label: noise correlation —contrasted-with→ signal correlation
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS DETERMINES THE SIGN OF THE EFFECT, NOT ITS SIZE. 'NOISE CORRELATIONS CAN EITHER ENHANCE OR IMPAIR CODING FIDELITY, DEPENDING ON HOW THE NOISE CORRELATION RELATES TO TUNING SIMILARITY (KNOWN AS SIGNAL CORRELATION) FOR EACH PAIR OF NEURONS.' A claim that noise correlations help or hurt is not well-formed until this relation is stated - so two papers reporting opposite effects can both be right, and a join on `noise correlation` alone would make them contradict. Q-476. · strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: correlated noise IMPAIRS coding between similarly tuned neurons and IMPROVES it between oppositely tuned ones. the same edge has opposite consequences depending on the second variable
span.quote: In such circuits, noise correlations can either enhance or impair coding fidelity, depending on how the noise correlation relates to tuning similarity (known as “signal correlation”) for each pair of neurons

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · task-relevant —contrasted-with→ task-irrelevant
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span said the motifs were heard equally often. This sentence names both AND GIVES THE DIFFERENTIA - 'the primary DIFFERENCE ... was thus the learned association between motifs and explicit behavioral choices' - so the contrast carries what it consists in. — strength of the relation: 1 — matched on familiarity and reward by design, differing only in whether the motif signalled a response - which is what makes the comparison interpretable
span.quote: All the motifs used during training were heard equally often in the context of the task and paired equally with reinforcement, but only the task-relevant motifs signaled the correct behavioral response on each trial. Thus, any effect of learning mediated directly by reinforcement should apply to all of the training motifs.

span.label: noise correlation —causes→ population code
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — and the effect cannot be predicted from the average responses of individual neurons, which is the paper's motivating point
span.quote: Thus, the relationship between signal and noise correlations has considerable impact on the fidelity of neural representations that cannot be predicted from the average responses of individual neurons.

span.label: population code —operationalised-as→ classification ratio
span.quote: We expressed this potential benefit as the “classification ratio,” which is simply the ratio of the MNLR classification accuracy with correlations intact to the classification accuracy without correlations (i.e. with trials shuffled, Experimental Procedures). Classification ratios greater than one indicate that correlations improve encoding while classification ratios less than one indicate that correlations impair encoding.

span.label: CLM —operationalised-as→ occasion setting

span.quote: The primary difference between the task-relevant and task-irrelevant motifs was thus the learned association between motifs and explicit behavioral choices.

span.label: Spearman correlation
span.quote: For task-relevant motifs, this relationship was negative (Spearman correlation coefficient: r = −0.15, p = 0.051, Fig. 4A ): larger signal correlations were accompanied by smaller noise correlations.

span.label: Pearson correlation
span.quote: Signal correlations were computed for each pair of neurons as the Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient between the mean (averaged over trials) firing rates to the four motifs within the task-relevant, task-irrelevant, and novel classes.

span.label: ANCOVA

span.label: repeated measures ANOVA

span.label: Friedman test
span.quote: We indeed found that task relevant motifs exhibit a higher classification ratio than the task-irrelevant or novel motifs (Friedman test, p = 0.018; Figure 6B ), consistent with our observations of the correlation structure.

span.label: Kruskal-Wallis test
span.quote: Among neuron pairs with strong positive signal correlations (greater than 0.4), the task-irrelevant and novel motifs evoked significantly larger noise correlations than the task-relevant motifs (Kruskal-Wallis Test, p = 0.0038; Figure 4D ).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Conversely, for neuron pairs with negative noise correlations, the classification ratio is larger for pairs with positive signal correlations than for pairs with negative signal correlations (t-test, p = 0.044; Figure 6A ).

This technique is particularly well-suited to our data because it can be applied to any number of neurons and any number of nominal categories (i.e. motifs).

span.quote: We show that learning produces stimulus specific changes in the pattern of inter-neuronal correlations that enhance the ability of neural populations to recognize signals relevant for behavior. This learning-dependent enhancement increases with population size.

span.quote: This suggests that the enhanced coding fidelity for task-relevant motifs results both from single neuron response properties and from correlations between neurons.

span.quote: What we observe, however, is very different. Only the task-relevant—motifs those that birds learned to associate with a particular pecking location—elicited neural population activity with a negative relationship between signal and noise correlations. In contrast, task-irrelevant motifs—those that birds never learned to associate with a particular pecking location—elicited neural population activity with a positive correlation relationship indistinguishable from that elicited by novel motifs that birds never heard while awake. Thus, learning-dependent changes in the inter-neuronal correlation patterns depend on associations formed between stimuli and behavior, rather than experience, familiarity, or reward contingency.

span.quote: To our knowledge, a negative relationship between signal and noise correlations has not previously been demonstrated. Theoretical studies, however, have predicted that changes to the sign of this relationship might underlie cognitive functions such as attention or learning ( Oram et al., 1998 ). We thus provide the first evidence to support this prediction: associative learning inverts this relationship, substantially enhancing population encoding of learned motifs.

span.label: noise correlation
span.quote: Pooling responses across distributed populations of similarly tuned neurons can enhance encoding fidelity by averaging out this response variability (known as “noise correlation”), but only the component of this noise that is independent between neurons

span.label: signal correlation
span.quote: In such circuits, noise correlations can either enhance or impair coding fidelity, depending on how the noise correlation relates to tuning similarity (known as “signal correlation”) for each pair of neurons

span.label: task-relevant vs task-irrelevant motif
span.quote: One motif in the pair (referred to as “task-relevant”) always signaled the correct behavioral response for the trial (i.e. whether to peck at the left or right port to receive food) and the other motif (referred to as “task-irrelevant”) never signaled the correct response

span.label: classification ratio
span.quote: We expressed this potential benefit as the “classification ratio,” which is simply the ratio of the MNLR classification accuracy with correlations intact to the classification accuracy without correlations

span.label: motif
span.quote: We constructed all stimuli from 12 motifs (stereotyped multi-note elements of natural starling song) recorded from the song repertoires of three adult European starlings.

span.label: inverted correlation structure
span.quote: Conversely, an inverted correlation structure in which noise correlations negatively co-vary with signal correlations can yield higher fidelity population representations relative to independent noise
